title: How Vestigial Organs Work
summary: Josh and Chuck discuss vestigial organs and traits, starting with pronunciation and the palmar grasp reflex, then covering the creationism-versus-evolution debate, Darwin and Robert Wiedersheim's list of vestigial parts, the appendix and its possible role as a bacteria reserve, wisdom teeth and tonsils, goosebumps (erector pili), the coccyx and atavisms, Darwin's point, ear-wiggling and ear muscles, the subclavius and palmaris longus muscles, neck ribs, sinuses and the vomeronasal organ, the nictitating membrane (third eyelid), body hair and the water ape theory, male nipples and vestigial ovaries/Müllerian remnants, flightless birds and cave animals, and whale and snake pelvis bones. The episode closes with Facebook listener questions about UK live shows, controversial topics, Sam the former staffer, Chuck's beard, coupons, grocery store donation drives, and bloopers.

segments.title: Opening banter and Jerry joke
segments.summary: Hosts open with silly banter about Jerry's supposed kidnapping, then correct the pronunciation of 'vestigial' and introduce the topic.

segments.title: Definition of vestigial traits and the palmar grasp reflex
segments.summary: Hosts define vestigial traits as remnants of ancestral function, using the palmar grasp reflex in babies as an example, and mention the foot grasp reflex.

segments.title: Vestigial definition, Darwin, and the creationism debate
segments.summary: Hosts explain that vestigial organs support evolution and note Darwin's view that vestigial structures may still have a function. They describe the conflict between creationists and scientists over the topic.

segments.title: Early vestigial lists and the appendix
segments.summary: Hosts mention Robert Wiedersheim's list of about 90 vestigial parts, many later disproven, and begin discussing the appendix as a supposedly useless organ.

segments.title: Appendix function and bacteria reserve
segments.summary: Hosts discuss the appendix's role in plant-eating animals and a proposed role as a reservoir of beneficial gut bacteria, and mention a study idea from Molly Edmonds.

segments.title: Wisdom teeth and tonsils
segments.summary: Hosts argue that wisdom teeth are evidence of evolution because jaws have shrunk with diet changes, causing impaction. They then discuss tonsils and the risks of removing them unnecessarily.

segments.title: Goosebumps and the erector pili muscles
segments.summary: Hosts explain goosebumps as a leftover from animals puffing up fur for warmth or defense, linked to the erector pili muscles.

segments.title: Horror movies and tangent
segments.summary: Hosts chat about Josh's horror movie kick and recommendations, including Pontypool on Netflix, and about their tangents.

segments.title: Tailbone, coccyx, and atavism
segments.summary: Hosts discuss the coccyx as a vestigial structure from the tail, distinguish it from atavisms such as a rare visible tail, and mention an unclear purpose for the coccyx.

segments.title: Darwin's point, ear muscles, and eyebrow tricks
segments.summary: Hosts discuss Darwin's point on the ear and ear muscles used for locating sounds, then joke about wiggling ears and eyebrows, and the subclavius and palmaris longus muscles.

segments.title: Neck ribs, sinuses, vomeronasal organ
segments.summary: Hosts describe neck ribs as left over from reptiles, discuss sinuses and their possible functions, and explain the vomeronasal organ, which is present but not connected to the brain.

segments.title: Third eyelid, body hair, nipples, and other examples
segments.summary: Hosts cover the third eyelid (plica semilunaris) and its reptile and bird origin, body hair and the water ape theory, male nipples, and vestigial ovaries in men and women, plus flightless birds and cave animals.

segments.title: Whale pelvis, dolphins, and listener mail
segments.summary: Hosts mention whale and snake pelvis bones and a Fresh Air interview about dolphins, then begin listener Facebook questions covering UK shows, controversial topics, Sam the former staffer, Chuck's beard, coupons, grocery store donation drives, and bloopers.

segments.title: Outro
segments.summary: Hosts give contact information and sign off.
